title: System design drills + behavioral finals
exp: Practice mid-senior designs (~35 min): URL shortener, notifications, rate limiter, checkout. Close with STAR stories.
pts: **URL shortener:** hash/counter IDs, Redis cache, store, rate limit, async analytics.
**Notifications:** channels, templates, outbox, retries, preferences, idempotency.
**Rate limiter:** token bucket/sliding window in Redis; 429 semantics.
**Checkout:** reserve inventory → pay → order; saga/compensations; payment idempotency.
pr: Design URL shortener on paper in 30 minutes
Record one incident STAR story aloud

viz.note: Whiteboard drill: pick one design daily. State requirements, API, data model, bottlenecks, and what you'd monitor in prod.

qa.q: Outline a notification service for email/SMS/push.
qa.a:
**Elevator Pitch:** API accepts notify requests with idempotency keys; persist outbox; workers per channel with retries/DLQ; template service; user preferences; provider adapters; metrics on send success/latency; never block the upstream order flow on provider latency.

**Under the Hood & Mechanics:** Operating at ~4 YOE requires knowing how the runtime behaves under memory and CPU constraints. Execution paths must preserve context without incurring unnecessary thread context switches or unneeded heap allocations.

**Production Failure Mode & Gotcha:** A classic failure mode in production is ignoring thread pool queue depths or unhandled transient network exceptions, leading to cascading failures across microservice boundaries.

**Senior Trade-Off Signal:** Always evaluate the trade-offs between simplicity, operational overhead, and scalability. Never over-engineer before profiling actual bottlenecks.

qa.q: Give a STAR story structure for a production incident.
qa.a:
**Elevator Pitch:** Situation: symptom + blast radius. Task: your ownership. Action: how you diagnosed (metrics/traces), mitigated, fixed root cause. Result: MTTR, error rate drop, follow-up (test, alert, postmortem).
